transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Well, nice to meet you, Dr. [Name]. I guess what brings me in is... I've just been taking on way too much lately. I volunteered for this historical society project, and I just sort of acted like I could run the entire fundraiser all by myself. I started drafting all these quilt designs, calling up a bunch of volunteers, drawing up schedules, and... well, I ended up promising all these deadlines that I just couldn't possibly meet. It just got totally out of hand.

Before this situation with the historical society project, would you say you normally tend to take on too many things and overcommit yourself, or is this kind of overambitious planning something new for you?

No, this isn't really how I normally do things. I usually know my limits. But this time... I don't know, I just truly believed my heritage quilt ideas were going to put our little town on the map. It felt like I had finally found the one thing that only I could make happen, you know? Like I was the only one who could see the vision and pull it all together. So I just jumped in headfirst.
During this time when you were working on the quilt project, how was your mood? Would you say you were feeling unusually happy, energetic, or 'up,' or have you been feeling down or anxious?

Well, at first... I felt really good. Almost glowing, I guess you could say. It was like every single idea I had was just wonderful and clear. I had so much energy for it. But... I did notice that if anyone questioned my plans or suggested something different, I got pretty snappish. I just felt like they were standing in the way of this great thing I was trying to do, and it really irritated me. So, I guess it was a mix of feeling really 'up' but also getting annoyed very easily.
Have you ever had periods like this before in your life—times when you felt unusually energetic, confident, and full of ideas, even if they didn't work out as planned?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had times where I felt good or got excited about a project, but nothing quite like this. Not where I felt like I was the only one who could do it, or where I just completely lost track of what was actually realistic. This felt... different.
Have you ever had periods where you felt significantly down, depressed, or hopeless for several days or weeks at a time?

Yes, I have. Actually, I'm in one of those periods right now. After the whole quilt project started falling apart—when the orders got backed up and I had all those conflicts with the volunteers—I just sort of crashed. I've been stuck in this really low, guilty place ever since. It's been about nine months now of just feeling completely down and hopeless.
When you were feeling really good and energetic about the quilt project—before things fell apart and you started feeling down—how long did that period of feeling 'up' last?

Well, let me think... that whole overdriven stretch with the historical society project went on for about five months. Yeah, it was right around five months of feeling like that before everything just fell apart.
Before this current nine-month period of feeling down and hopeless, have you had other times in your life when you felt depressed or very low for several weeks or months at a time?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had normal ups and downs, like anyone, but I've never had a period where I felt this low for this long before. This is really the first time I've been stuck in something like this.

You mentioned this is the first time you've felt this low for this long. But going back further in your life—say, before this quilt project started—have you ever had any other stretches of feeling depressed, sad, or down that lasted for weeks or even just a couple of weeks?

No, I really haven't. I mean, sure, I've had bad days here and there, like if someone passed away or something upsetting happened, but... no, nothing like this. I've never had a stretch where I felt down or depressed for weeks at a time before all of this started. This is completely new for me.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a first episode of major depressive disorder lasting 9 months with significant functional impairment (guilt, hopelessness). While she experienced a 5-month period of elevated mood, increased goal-directed activity, and irritability preceding the depression, this appears to be a single hypomanic-like episode without prior history of mood episodes. The absence of documented prior depressive or manic episodes, combined with the current prominent depressive presentation and functional impairment, is more consistent with MDD than bipolar disorder.
